children: Malaysia's central bank is expected to leave its overnight policy rate unchanged this week, with investors watching for signals of a possible rate increase in January, BofA Securities economists Kai Wei Ang and Rahul Bajoria say in a note. Their base case is for an extended pause, though they flag the risk of a 25-basis-point rate increase in March if higher costs feed into consumer prices or economic conditions warrant tighter policy. Inflation is expected to remain around 2%-2.2% in 2027, while government measures should help contain price pressures, the economists add. BofA thinks there is little chance of a smaller 12.5 basis-point increase, given the markets' sensitivity to changes in the central bank's messaging. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
